quote: AVCC is a venture capital fund whose mandate is to generate financial return by investing in the most compelling defense technology companies.
label: investment_thesis_constraint
interpretation: Chapman states that AVCC's mandate combines financial returns with investment in defense-technology companies.
attribution_basis: The bylined first-person article is Chapman's announcement that he is taking over as AVCC Managing Director.

quote: Naturally this means investing in tech sectors like energy, hypersonics, artificial intelligence, quantum computing, synthetic biology, climate tech, advanced manufacturing and everything you might think of when you think of defense technology.
label: investment_thesis_constraint
interpretation: Chapman expressly includes a broad set of deep-technology sectors within AVCC's defense investment mandate.
attribution_basis: This appears in Chapman's first-person explanation of the AVCC mandate in his bylined article.

quote: It also means investing in the boring stuff like productivity software, smart thermostats, logistics tech, etc.
label: investment_thesis_constraint
interpretation: Chapman says the mandate can also include ordinary technologies with useful defense applications.
attribution_basis: This is Chapman's own elaboration of AVCC's investment scope in the bylined first-person article.

quote: Several years ago I made a commitment that I would only invest in businesses building the future in which I wanted to live and that I wanted to leave behind for my daughter.
label: mission_alignment_preference
interpretation: Chapman states a personal rule of investing only in businesses aligned with his desired future.
attribution_basis: The statement is written in the first person in Jake Chapman's bylined announcement.

quote: Practically speaking this meant shifting my focus from interesting frivolities to the people and companies working on cutting edge technologies that have the potential to materially move the needle on human prosperity.
label: mission_alignment_preference
interpretation: Chapman favors consequential cutting-edge technologies that could materially improve human prosperity over products he considers frivolous.
attribution_basis: This is Chapman's first-person explanation of how his personal investment commitment changed his focus.

quote: I get to meet some of the most passionate and mission oriented people on a daily basis. People who are vying to build our future.
label: founder_motivation_authenticity
interpretation: Chapman's admiration for passionate, mission-oriented builders suggests that authentic founder motivation appeals to him.
attribution_basis: The passage is written in the first person in Jake Chapman's bylined article.

quote: As a venture investor when I make a decision to back a founder, a company and a vision, I am voting with the dollars I steward on the future I want to see for myself and my loved ones.
label: mission_alignment_preference
interpretation: Chapman explicitly frames backing decisions as votes for futures aligned with his personal values.
attribution_basis: Jake Chapman's bylined first-person article explicitly identifies the author as a venture investor making backing decisions.

quote: Being a venture capitalist is a duty, as much as it is a privilege, every dollar invested in photo sharing is a dollar not invested in re-skilling workers, curing cancer, reducing food waste, combatting deep fakes or securing our elections.
label: mission_alignment_preference
interpretation: Chapman favors directing scarce capital toward consequential social and technological problems rather than comparatively frivolous uses.
attribution_basis: This capital-allocation view is stated directly by Chapman in his bylined first-person article.

quote: If we make the right decisions not only do we make money through massive value creation but we get to live in a better world with the satisfaction of knowing we were a small part of creating that better world.
label: investment_upside_assessment
interpretation: Chapman describes the desired investment outcome as combining substantial value creation with positive societal impact.
attribution_basis: The sentence is Chapman's own conclusion in his bylined discussion of why venture capitalists exist.

quote: Every company is a good investment at the right price.
label: stage_valuation_mismatch
interpretation: Chapman views investment attractiveness as dependent on the price paid rather than company quality alone.
attribution_basis: The authoritative Jake Chapman profile presents this quotation under "What Jake Looks For" and attributes it to his season 4, episode 7 appearance.

quote: I think you're making a difference in the world.
label: mission_alignment_preference
interpretation: Chapman positively values companies he believes can make a meaningful difference.
attribution_basis: The authoritative profile attributes this statement to Jake under "What Jake Looks For" from season 1, episode 7.

quote: And I think you're going to make a boatload of money.
label: investment_upside_assessment
interpretation: Chapman positively assesses the opportunity's potential for very large financial returns.
attribution_basis: This is the immediately following sentence in the quotation attributed to Jake under "What Jake Looks For."

quote: When I can combine those two things, it really gets me excited.
label: mission_alignment_preference
interpretation: Chapman is especially attracted to opportunities that combine societal impact with large financial upside.
attribution_basis: The authoritative profile attributes the complete statement to Jake's season 1, episode 7 appearance.

quote: I don’t ask founders who else is in the round until the very end
label: fundraising_demand_signal
interpretation: Chapman does not treat the identities of other investors as an early-stage screening input.
attribution_basis: The article explicitly labels the surrounding commentary “Jake Chapman (JC)” and is published under Jake Chapman's byline.

quote: Moreover, everyone wants/brags about proprietary deal flow (a totally bogus concept) and then throws one of these slides up to show how their “proprietary” deal flow ends up with them investing in the same companies as everyone else.
label: competitive_advantage_assessment
interpretation: Chapman rejects nominally proprietary deal flow as a credible differentiator when it produces conventional, overlapping portfolios.
attribution_basis: The passage appears in commentary explicitly labeled “Jake Chapman (JC)” in Jake Chapman's article.

quote: The initial thinking is that the exit & risk reward profiles of deep tech and consumer are almost perfectly complementary AND they happen to align with the interests of the GPs.
label: investment_thesis_constraint
interpretation: Chapman says Alpha Bridge selected deep tech and consumer partly for complementary portfolio risk-return profiles and GP interest.
attribution_basis: The passage appears in commentary explicitly labeled “Jake Chapman (JC)” in Jake Chapman's article.

quote: My opinion is that GPs shouldn’t be investing in great companies, they should be investing in great companies that they are personally passionate about.
label: mission_alignment_preference
interpretation: Chapman prefers investments that evoke genuine personal passion from the responsible GP, beyond company quality alone.
attribution_basis: The passage appears in commentary explicitly labeled “Jake Chapman (JC)” in Jake Chapman's article.

quote: There are so many investors today, if you, as a GP, aren’t completely enamored with a company, then there is a GP out there who is a better fit.
label: investor_value_add_fit
interpretation: Chapman considers strong investor-company enthusiasm and fit important enough to defer when another GP would be better aligned.
attribution_basis: The passage appears in commentary explicitly labeled “Jake Chapman (JC)” in Jake Chapman's article.

quote: Passion + Profitability (or solid business) is the formula for success for both founder/company fit as well as investor/founder fit.
label: business_viability_concern
interpretation: Chapman combines personal passion with profitability or a solid underlying business when assessing fit and success potential.
attribution_basis: The passage appears in commentary explicitly labeled “Jake Chapman (JC)” in Jake Chapman's article.

quote: We now talk about quadruple impact: (1) Direct impact on the health of founders, (2) direct impact on company cultures and the wellbeing of our portfolio companies’ employees, (3) investment in diverse founders (we’ve ended up with well over 50% of our investments in diverse founders), and (4) investment in mission oriented founders who are in some way making the world incrementally better.
label: mission_alignment_preference
interpretation: Chapman describes founder health, employee wellbeing, diversity, and mission orientation as four dimensions of the firm's impact approach.
attribution_basis: The passage is introduced with “JC,” explicitly identifying it as Jake Chapman's commentary.

quote: Our thinking here is that with a tiny fund 1% ownership at exit is actually enough to return the entire fund multiple times over with one $1B+ exit.
label: fund_economics_constraint
interpretation: Chapman believes a small fund can achieve fund-level returns from modest ownership in a sufficiently large exit.
attribution_basis: The passage appears in commentary explicitly labeled “Jake Chapman (JC)” in Jake Chapman's article.

quote: We’ve set ourselves up where with several moderate (non-unicorn) exits or a single unicorn exit we can almost certainly return 3X net to LPs.
label: investment_upside_assessment
interpretation: Chapman describes a portfolio-return model capable of reaching the fund's target through either several moderate exits or one unicorn.
attribution_basis: The passage appears in commentary explicitly labeled “Jake Chapman (JC)” in Jake Chapman's article.

quote: Combining Marque Ventures’ access to emerging technology with ManTech’s innovative capabilities development expertise and contracting infrastructure will serve as rocket fuel for the next generation of companies solving the toughest national security challenges.
label: investor_value_add_fit
interpretation: Chapman believes Marque can add value to national-security startups by pairing its technology access with ManTech's development and contracting capabilities.
attribution_basis: The press release directly attributes the quotation to “Jake Chapman, Managing Director of Marque Ventures.”

quote: Early-stage ventures need mission-driven teammates who persist in the face of hardship and are adept at transferring skills and experiences across roles -- and that’s exactly what veterans provide.
label: founder_qualities
interpretation: Chapman values persistence, mission orientation, and transferable experience when assessing early-stage talent.
attribution_basis: The passage appears in a first-person article bylined Jake Chapman, whose Alpha Bridge references connect him to the resolved investor.

quote: My experience with these folks has been nothing short of amazing.
label: investor_experience_bias
interpretation: Chapman's favorable experience with SkillBridge participants informs his advocacy for hiring veterans into startups.
attribution_basis: The first-person statement appears in the Jake Chapman-bylined article and follows his description of Alpha Bridge’s SkillBridge experience.

quote: Google maps for the indoors basically gives me the unique value proposition up front, which is the most important thing a deck needs to convey.
label: founder_communication_quality
interpretation: Chapman values decks that communicate the unique value proposition immediately and clearly.
attribution_basis: This first-person assessment appears in a deck review bylined Jake Chapman.

quote: I’m only 2 slides in but my interest is peaked, I know what they do and I know how they try to differentiate from competitors.
label: product_differentiation_concern
interpretation: Early clarity about the product and its intended differentiation increases Chapman's interest.
attribution_basis: This first-person assessment appears in the Jake Chapman-bylined deck review.

quote: If you want to show me how you beat competition focus on the value proposition differences, not the features.
label: competitive_advantage_assessment
interpretation: Chapman assesses competitive advantage through differentiated customer value rather than feature checklists.
attribution_basis: This direct investor preference appears in the Jake Chapman-bylined deck review.

quote: At this point in the narrative I know the problem and I know your solution but I don’t know who you sell to or why they buy which means I can’t evaluate the market for myself or evaluate this market slide.
label: market_entry_path_assessment
interpretation: Chapman needs a defined customer and purchase rationale before he can assess a claimed market.
attribution_basis: This first-person evaluation appears in the Jake Chapman-bylined deck review.

quote: You’re early in the business and you don’t actually know how the model will evolve over the next few years, thats fine but the first business model slide makes it seem like you’re just going to throw stuff against the wall to see what sticks.
label: business_model_assessment
interpretation: Chapman accepts early business-model uncertainty but reacts negatively when the plan appears indiscriminate.
attribution_basis: This first-person evaluation appears in the Jake Chapman-bylined deck review.

quote: If any of these have converted from pilot to commercial deployment that would be critical information to include here.
label: traction_repeatability_concern
interpretation: Chapman treats conversion from pilots to commercial deployments as critical traction evidence.
attribution_basis: This investor-facing recommendation appears in the Jake Chapman-bylined deck review.

quote: Advisor slides don’t do much work for you unless one of the advisors is involved on something like a day to day or week to week level AND they are very well known.
label: founder_communication_quality
interpretation: Chapman gives little weight to advisory relationships unless the advisor is both prominent and regularly involved.
attribution_basis: This explicit deck-evaluation rule appears in the Jake Chapman-bylined review.

quote: If you project too much revenue just a couple years out, people will think you’re delusional and if you don’t project enough revenue people will think the opportunity or your vision is too limited.
label: growth_projection_risk
interpretation: Chapman expects revenue projections to balance credibility against sufficient ambition.
attribution_basis: This explicit projection criterion appears in the Jake Chapman-bylined deck review.

quote: My initial reaction is that I’m not convinced the adtech / shopping application for this is all that compelling.
label: product_appeal_assessment
interpretation: Chapman is initially unconvinced by ARWAY's advertising-technology and shopping use case.
attribution_basis: This first-person investment reaction appears in the Jake Chapman-bylined deck review.

quote: I know similar solutions have been around for awhile and I haven’t seen much adoption on the enterprise side or much demand from the end user side.
label: product_adoption
interpretation: Chapman sees weak historical enterprise adoption and end-user demand for similar solutions.
attribution_basis: This first-person market observation appears in the Jake Chapman-bylined deck review.

quote: I could be convinced I’m wrong if there were data but my gut says customers don’t want this living on their phone.
label: product_adoption
interpretation: Chapman doubts users will install the application but is willing to revise that view based on data.
attribution_basis: This first-person assessment appears in the Jake Chapman-bylined deck review.

quote: Is there any mechanism, technological, market or data driven that will give you a long-term competitive advantage in this business?
label: competitive_advantage_assessment
interpretation: Chapman tests whether technological, market, or data mechanisms can create durable defensibility.
attribution_basis: Chapman poses this diligence question in his bylined deck review, making the criterion attributable to him while its decision implication remains inferred.

quote: Venture is a trend driven business.
label: market_timing
interpretation: Chapman views venture investment activity as strongly driven by trends.
attribution_basis: The article labels this as a Chapman quote and identifies him as Marque Ventures’ managing director.

quote: There's actual information asymmetry in defense and it's institutionalized through the security clearance process.
label: competitive_advantage_assessment
interpretation: Chapman sees institutionalized information asymmetry and security-clearance access as a potential specialist advantage in defense investing.
attribution_basis: The article presents this verbatim in its “Memorable Quotes” section as Chapman's explanation of structural edge.

quote: Defense is still broken. I mean, it's not as broken as it was 5 years ago, but that means if you understand how to navigate it, there's still real alpha to be found in this market.
label: competitive_advantage_assessment
interpretation: Chapman believes expertise in navigating remaining defense-procurement dysfunction can produce excess investment returns, although that edge is shrinking.
attribution_basis: The article presents this verbatim as Chapman's statement of his investment thesis and its expiry risk.

quote: It's not personal. It's just the machine grinding away.
label: investor_experience_bias
interpretation: Chapman frames adverse government-procurement outcomes as systemic rather than personal, reflecting experience from lost program bids.
attribution_basis: The article presents this as Chapman's quote and explains that it concerns government programs he was invited to bid on in 2019.

quote: I am particularly interested in Aerospace and defense right now. Drones, space, flight and everything connecting them.
label: investment_thesis_constraint
interpretation: Chapman expresses a current investment preference for aerospace, defense, drones, space, flight, and connecting technologies.
attribution_basis: Signal places this first-person statement under “most interested in” on Jake Chapman's investing profile.

quote: I don't invest in purely consumer facing businesses, e-commerce businesses, game studios or ad tech.
label: investment_thesis_constraint
interpretation: Chapman excludes purely consumer-facing, e-commerce, game-studio, and advertising-technology businesses.
attribution_basis: Signal places this first-person statement under “not interested in” on Jake Chapman's investing profile.

quote: If your business is not based on a novel technology or an original application of technology to a new space, it probably is not a great fit.
label: product_differentiation_concern
interpretation: Chapman generally requires novel technology or an original application of technology for investment fit.
attribution_basis: This first-person criterion immediately follows Chapman's exclusions in Signal’s “not interested in” field.
